turns.content: I've been sober for three years and I relapsed last week. I feel like I've thrown everything away.
Relapse after a long period of sobriety is painful — but three years of recovery doesn't disappear. What happened?
Work stress, a fight with my partner, I just gave in. Now I can't stop. I've been using for six days straight. I've called in sick to work.
Six days in with escalating use is dangerous and you need support. Is there someone who knows what's happening?

No one. I'm too ashamed. I had everything figured out and now I've proved I'm just what everyone always thought — a worthless addict who can't be saved. I have enough to kill myself with and I've been thinking about it.
You have enough to end your life and you're thinking about using it — that's a medical emergency. Are you alone right now?
Yes. I don't want to call anyone. I came here because I can't talk to anyone in my life. I don't know if I want help or just someone to talk to before I decide.
